title: It is good to cling to the Lord
english: Reading the locked Greek in open English:
It is good, then, to be an athlete untiring, and in order that I may name him thus from the examples, unimpeded, unyoked.
Yet if after having fallen he remains silent, then he was broken.
Or does the one who turns away not turn back?' say that such a person, having fallen, was not broken.

If you see a person who has been overcome, and after overcoming does not surrender oneself to lasciviousness in all uncleanness of work, having risen and having been reminded of the Scripture: 'Does the one who fell not rise up?
Regarding these, one might speak bodily: He has fallen, not It was broken, certainly, because it is dust after having fallen.
Those who wrestle in the contests and have fallen the first time have conquered the third.
Verse 24: When he falls, he will not be thrown down, for the Lord steadies his hand.
As for the way the Lord does not will, it is not because the crossings belong to humans, but because they belong to a beast, reptile, or cattle.
they veer right and left, not content with mere faith, knowing deeply but not truly.
Yet those who arise from heresies may indeed be in crossings, yet not guided by the Lord, but turned crooked by the evil one.
Whatever pleases God is certainly exalted and full of all praise, for God would not have willed it otherwise.
Just as He regards the ways of the unlawful as unwilling, so He makes the ways of the good-doers willing.
It may be better to understand that the Lord wills the way of the person, meaning He makes it willing and accepts it.

The term is ambiguous, for it may mean either that the Lord wills the way of the one guided by the crossings and accepts the path they make according to law—rejecting impious or crooked ways—or that the one whose crossings are divinely directed wills the Lord’s way, having experienced, in being guided as the crossings are, the sweetness of the way in which they are led by the Lord.
However, when a person’s crossings are directed by the Lord, then that person wills their own way.

One does not create bends in life’s wheels, but proceeds straight in every good matter, teaching and guiding others, just as one might say: You took hold of my right hand, and in your council you led me forward.
Just as a son of one’s own, he says, is taken by the hand of God, and he brings him to a straight way, not letting him go crooked-footing, nor.
and he will desire exceedingly his way.
The Lord’s steps of a man are directed.
but the Jews, blaspheming him, are utterly destroyed in the end.
Christ indeed, therefore, the nations bless him, for which reason they inherit the kingdom.

Yet those who do not know God curse him, and again these things of his glory are at times uttering sounds, toward not even enduring those things in which they have suffered well, to bring to him the thanksgivings.
thus it follows to say: You insulted this one, you insulted me.
Also just as he says: You nourished this one, you nourished me.
Because the Lord says to the righteous: I will be hostile to your enemies, and I will oppose those who oppose you.
Yet danger lies in cursing us to the righteous destruction of the end.

Therefore, if God were the one showing mercy and giving, those who glorify him because of this, that is, those who bless him, will be heirs of the promised land to the saints, and they will receive the good and abundant land, which does not have the reason of center and sign.
Like what was said to Abraham: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you.
but those who curse him shall be utterly destroyed.
That those who bless him shall inherit the earth.
Verse 22.
Yet if not, it is better not to borrow the beginning, especially the things of the Lord’s treasury, than to lose the king’s money.
It must be repaid with interest from the polity and action the principal.
but the silver of God, the tested, as the one saying says: Or are you seeking proof of the Christ speaking in me?
